disease_label_per_paper: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis secondary to Salmonella spp. in decompensated liver cirrhosis
presentation_summary: 63-year-old man with hepatitis C cirrhosis, prior variceal upper GI bleed, unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma, and no prior SBP presented with 48 hours of abdominal distension, worsening jaundice, and lower-extremity swelling.
Vital signs were within normal limits. Exam showed scleral icterus, tense ascites, bilateral pitting edema, and no asterixis.

Labs showed WBC 18.8 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL, platelets 200 x10^9/L, INR 1.9, sodium 123 mmol/L, potassium 5.5 mmol/L, albumin 1.6 g/dL, CRP 70 mg/L, AST 129 U/L, ALT 71 U/L, and bilirubin 6.3 mg/dL.

Ultrasound showed cirrhosis and large-volume ascites with portal vein occlusion/cavernous transformation. Initial paracentesis removed 5.0 L of clear straw-colored fluid; ascitic PMN count was 2,983 with protein 1.6 g/dL, albumin <0.6 g/dL, LDH 182 U/L, glucose 43 mg/dL, and SAAG >1.1 g/dL.
Salmonella enterica culture, susceptibility, repeat culture negativity, and clinical response are confirmatory/non-ranking.
